events.what: Choi and Lee prove that for each fixed d, Newman's conjecture holds for a density-1 set of moduli with exactly d distinct prime divisors (arXiv:2212.00636; v2 of 29 May 2025 changed the title; published Adv. Math. 477 (2025) 110367)

judgement.doubts: The record dated the event to the May 2025 v2 only because v2 was the version published; its own competing_reading says only the title change is documented and it could not diff v1 against v2. Under F7 a revision moves the date only when the record shows new mathematics, and it shows none, so the first written argument is the 1 Dec 2022 v1, before the snapshot. Even if dated after the snapshot it would be a case (partial), and a pre-snapshot partial result is not open_stale, so the status is open. If a v1/v2 diff showed the density-1 theorem was new in 2025, the status would go back to partial.

corrections.why: F7: the record says v1 of arXiv:2212.00636 was submitted 1 December 2022, and the only documented change in the 29 May 2025 v2 is the title ('only the title changed, per the arXiv comment field'). Journal acceptance does not re-date the work, so the case result predates the snapshot. A pre-snapshot partial result leaves the problem open, not open_stale.
other: with status open and no post-snapshot event left, the direction is null (§4 step 6).
F7: once the Choi–Lee result is dated to 2022, the record describes no post-snapshot event bearing on the bullet.
